newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Major Czech, Slovak steel firms discuss cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Major Czech, Slovak steel firms discuss cooperation.

text.p: Slovakia's leading steel producer VSZ a.s. and Czech steel maker Nova Hut on Tuesday discussed mutual cooperation in the field of purchasing raw materials, a statement issued by VSZ said on Wednesday.
The statement said the two companies also discussed possible co-ordination in completion of unspecified deliveries.
No final cooperation treaty came out of the talks, the statement said, but added that the two agreed on future negotiations at summit level.

VSZ press officials declined to comment further on the negotiations, and added the date for future talks had not yet been set. It was not clear whether the future talks would include possible VSZ capital participation in Nova Hut.
Nova Hut officials were not immediately available for comment.

Earlier this month the Czech privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), set two tenders for stakes of roughly 18.3 percent in two largest Czech steelworks, Nova Hut and Vitkovice, saying priority will be given to participants who display practical experience in similar transactions.

VSZ has been in talks aimed at acquiring a 19 percent stake in both the Vitkovice and Nova Hut steel mills and has established contacts with Polish mill Huta Katowice, one of Poland's steel largest companies.
VSZ's strategy is to become a multi-national corporation, through creation of a strong and integrated group of central European mills.

In addition, VSZ has already bought major stakes in firms ranging from banking and insurance subjects, and even the Czech soccer team Sparta Praha, at an estimated total cost of about five billion crowns.

Earlier this year VSZ and Czech steel mill Trinecke Zelezarny signed an agreement according to which VSZ may acquire 20 percent of Trinecke, which may acquire 10 percent of VSZ within an unspecified period of time.
